Chapter 3: The Role of Emotion and Motivation in Lasting Change
Even if you’ve set up the right environment and you know what habits you want to build, real change isn’t always a smooth ride, is it? Some days, motivation is sky-high—a fresh start feels so close you can almost touch it. But then there are those tougher days, when old habits creep back in, and stress or exhaustion make it so tempting to slip into familiar routines.
Think about a college student who’s decided she wants to exercise more. At first, she’s all in—waking up early, lacing up her sneakers, heading out for a run before class. But as the semester gets busier and the weather turns chilly, her determination starts to fade. She keeps telling herself, “I’ll get back to it tomorrow,” but somehow, tomorrow never seems to arrive. If you’ve ever tried to make a lasting change, you probably know that cycle of hope and disappointment all too well.
Here’s what really stands out: motivation isn’t something you can count on to always be there. It comes and goes, depending on your mood, your energy, and what’s going on around you. So many people wait for that perfect moment—thinking, “I’ll change when I feel ready.” But honestly, waiting for motivation? It usually leads nowhere.
The real trick is to build systems that make taking action easier, even on those days when you’re just not feeling it. One way to do this is by focusing on small wins—those tiny steps forward that help you feel progress and build momentum. For example, if you want to eat healthier, you might just start with adding one serving of veggies to your dinner. Not a complete overhaul, just a small, doable change. Or, if you’re hoping to write more, maybe you commit to just five minutes a day. Over time, those little bits of effort add up to something much bigger.
Now, let’s talk about emotion. It’s a huge part of this whole process. When you feel proud, satisfied, or accomplished after taking a positive step, those good feelings reinforce your new habits and make them stick. On the flip side, negative emotions—like frustration or disappointment—can pull you right back into old patterns and make change feel impossible. That’s why it’s so important to celebrate every bit of progress, no matter how small, and to be gentle with yourself when setbacks happen.
Over time, you start to see that lasting change isn’t about being perfect—it’s about sticking with it. It’s about showing up, day after day, even when your motivation isn’t where you want it to be and the future looks a little uncertain. By focusing on small actions and cheering yourself on for each step, you start to build habits that actually last. And in the end, that’s what creates real growth and resilience.
